abstract.p: The Alia musica is transmitted in 14 manuscripts from different centuries and locations, either presenting the full text or excerpts and compilations. Respecting the manuscripts as documents of individual scribal intentions or specific institutional demands, each extant copy from the Alia musica is edited separately. The apparatus represents the differences between the manuscript and the edited texts and reports particuliarities regarding the text’s materiality and semantics. A separate view presents all interlinear and marginal glosses. The individual readings of the different manuscripts can be compared using the synopsis. Quotations or paraphrases from earlier texts can be compared with their source texts. The translations provided refer to the individual text of each manuscript.

The critical apparatus concerns this manuscript alone. It records all differences between the edited text and the manuscript, together with observations on the text’s materiality and semantics. Hover over the edited text to highlight the differences.
All interlinear and marginal glosses in the manuscript.

All quotations and paraphrases of ancient or medieval texts are displayed alongside their sources. The source texts are presented in a separate column, following the relevant reference editions. Passages shown in grey have no readily identifiable counterpart in the relevant source text.
The synopsis compares the readings of each sentence across the manuscript tradition. Hover over the edited text to display the corresponding readings.
An English translation of the text as transmitted in this manuscript.

p.seg: De armonica consideratione Boetius ita disseruit:
Quia neque solum in terminis speculationem proporcionis habet, neque solum in differentiis, sed in utrisque communiter,
querit enim ut quemadmodum sunt ad se extremi termini, sic maioris ad medium differentia contra differentiam medietatis ad ultimum.
Ipsarum quoque musicarum consonantiarum, quas symphonias nominant, proporciones in hac poene sola medietate frequenter inuenies.
Namque symphonia diatesseron que princeps est et quodammodo uim obtinet elementi, in eiusmodi armonicis medietatibus inuenitur, ut sunt VI. ad VIII.
Sunt ergo huiusmodi medietatis termini, quorum extremi sint dupli, et alii quorum extremi sint tripli, ita:
Duodenarius igitur ad senarium duplus est;
et in alia dispositione XII. ad IIII. triplus est.
Horum diferentias colligamus et ad se inuicem comparemus, epytrita proportio, id est diatesseron symphonia colligitur.
Inter VI. enim et XII. senarius est, et inter IIII. et XII. octonarius; qui scilicet octonarius ad senarium sesquiterciam efficit proportionem.
In eadem quoque medietate et diapente symphonia componitur.
In duplici, uidelicet XII. ad VIII. et in triplici VI. ad IIII. sesqualtera est.
Post hunc autem diapason consonantia est, ut VI. ad XII.
In triplici quoque dispositione simul diapente et diapason symphonia componitur, ut sunt
Et quoniam triplus duas continet consonantias, diapente scilicet ac diapason, in differentiis eiusdem triplicis eundem triplum reperiemus.
Nam inter VI. et VIIII. ternarius differentia est, et inter VIII. et XVIII. nouenarius, qui ad ternarium triplus est.
In dupla vero proportione, major terminus differentiam sui et medii termini triplus est,
et rursus minor terminus ad differentiam sui et medii termini triplus est.
Nam inter VIII. et XII. quaternarius est, qui ad eundem duodenarium triplus est, et inter VI. et VIII. binarius, qui rursus ad eundem senarium triplus est.
